 Follow Pennsylvania minimum wage increase coming? What Shapiro says will happen
 Maria Francis, USA TODAY NETWORK Updated Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:33 PM UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Pennsylvania minimum wage increase coming? What Shapiro says will happen Pennsylvania workers could finally be getting a raise. After 17 years with the state's minimum wage stuck at $7.25 an hour, Gov. Josh Shapiro says that's about to change.
 "We will raise the minimum wage," Shapiro said Wednesday , one day after an election that gave Democrats control of the Pennsylvania Senate and strengthened their majority in the state House.
 Democrats are set to hold a 26-24 majority in the state Senate, giving the party control of the governor's office and both chambers of the legislature. Democratic leaders indicated Wednesday that raising the minimum wage will be among their early priorities.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement No new minimum wage has been signed into law, and exactly how much Pennsylvania's minimum wage will increase, and when workers will see that raise, still needs to be worked out.
 Here's what Pennsylvania workers should know.
 What is the minimum wage in Pennsylvania in 2026?
 Pennsylvania's minimum wage is currently $7.25 an hour, the same as the federal minimum wage. It has been stuck there since 2009. More than half a million Pennsylvanians earn less than $15 an hour, according to the Shapiro administration.
 The administration says the purchasing power of the state's $7.25 minimum wage has fallen by more than 30% since 2009.
 Is Pennsylvania's minimum wage going up?
 It appears significantly more likely following Tuesday's election, but a new minimum wage has not yet become law. Shapiro was unequivocal Wednesday about what he expects the new Democratic-controlled government to accomplish.
 Advertisement Advertisement "We will raise the minimum wage," he said while laying out priorities that also included mass transit funding and housing. Democratic lawmakers have also signaled that minimum-wage legislation will be among the first measures they pursue when the new legislature convenes.
 That represents a major shift in Harrisburg. The Democratic-controlled House has repeatedly passed legislation to raise the wage, but those efforts stalled in the previously Republican-controlled Senate.
 Will Pennsylvania's minimum wage increase to $15 an hour?
 Shapiro has repeatedly called for Pennsylvania to adopt a $15-an-hour minimum wage, but $15 has not yet been enacted into law. In March, the Pennsylvania House approved H.B. 2189 , a plan that would gradually raise the minimum wage rather than immediately jump from $7.25 to $15.
 Under that proposal, the minimum wage would rise to $11 an hour, increase to $13 in 2028 and reach $15 in 2029. Future increases would be tied to the cost of living.
 Advertisement Advertisement Counties would also have the option of moving to $15 earlier under the House-approved plan.
 However, that shouldn't be confused with a finalized schedule for the new Democratic legislature. Lawmakers still need to determine the details of the legislation they'll send to Shapiro.
 When could Pennsylvania's minimum wage increase?
 That's one of the biggest unanswered questions. Democratic leaders said minimum-wage legislation will be an early priority, and Shapiro said his party will soon announce an agenda for its first 100 days of governing.
 But neither an effective date nor a final wage has been established.
 Democrats also aren't necessarily united yet on what the final number should be. State Sen. Vincent Hughes said Wednesday that he wants to "double that sucker," while other Democratic lawmakers acknowledged that members have different opinions on exactly how high Pennsylvania's minimum wage should go.
 Advertisement Advertisement Doubling Pennsylvania's current $7.25 minimum wage would put it at $14.50 an hour.
 Why hasn't Pennsylvania raised its minimum wage?
 For years, the biggest obstacle has been disagreement between the two chambers of Pennsylvania's divided legislature. The Democratic-controlled House passed minimum-wage legislation three times in recent years, while the Republican-controlled Senate declined to advance it, according to the Shapiro administration.
 After the House approved H.B. 2189 in March, Shapiro urged Senate Republicans to bring the measure up for a vote and send it to his desk.
 Tuesday's election changes that political equation. Democrats flipped enough seats to take a 26-24 majority in the state Senate while expanding their control of the state House.
 When was the last Pennsylvania minimum wage increase?
 Pennsylvania workers have been waiting a long time. The state's minimum wage reached its current $7.25-an-hour level in 2009 when the federal minimum wage increased to the same amount. Pennsylvania lawmakers last voted to increase the state minimum wage in 2006.
 Advertisement Advertisement Since then, Pennsylvania's neighboring states have increased their minimum wages while Pennsylvania remained at $7.25.
 How much will Pennsylvania's minimum wage be in 2027?
 Right now, there isn't a definitive number. Shapiro is promising that Pennsylvania will raise the minimum wage, and Democrats will enter the new legislative session controlling both chambers. But lawmakers still have to agree on the amount, timetable and details of the legislation before Shapiro can sign it into law.
 The previous House-approved proposal provides a roadmap toward a $15 minimum wage, but it does not guarantee that the incoming legislature will ultimately adopt the same schedule.
 Maria Francis is a Pennsylvania-based journalist covering trending and breaking topics across the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast regions for USA Today Network. Reach her at mfrancis@usatodayco.com.
